signal: Great Question raised a $13M Series A led by Inovia (Nov 2025) and shipped an MCP in March 2026 to run research from AI tools like Claude and Cursor

email.subject1: a signal play for Great Question
email.body1:
Tucker, saw Great Question closed its $13M Series A and just shipped the MCP so teams can run research straight from Claude and Cursor.

Scaling post-raise usually means more research-led accounts in play than the team can cover before new reps ramp. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Great Question off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Tucker, quick follow-up for Great Question.

Post-Series-A, board expectations on pipeline jump faster than headcount can, and most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to hit the new number. The gap surfaces late, then it is a scramble to save the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Great Question needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Tucker, last bit of proof for Great Question.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks.

I pulled a benchmark of how Great Question's reply rate likely compares to other Series-A startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Tucker, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything right after a raise, and that stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a Series-A motion? I will tailor it to Great Question either way.
